clue.text: Moral compass, contrary to biology etc.

parts.note: con is a word for an argument against, as in pros and cons
biology, chemistry and the like are sciences

explanation.surface: Someone claims that having a moral compass goes against the findings of biology and other sciences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'etc.' signals that biology is just one example of the wider category, which is the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Your inner sense of right and wrong guides your behaviour the way a compass guides a traveller.

clue.text: Tents being affected

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is a single noun for a group of tents
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of tents pitched together
second meaning: theatrical, exaggerated or mannered in style

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tents damaged by weather; 'being affected' is really a description of showy, mannered behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of pitched shelters forms an encampment, and an exaggerated, theatrical manner is also described with this word.

clue.text: Notes describing Everyman: ultimately tolerable square

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one piece is drawn around another

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes give two Ns
the setter refers to themself, so Everyman is I

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Some notes describe the crossword setter Everyman as, in the end, a tolerably square, old-fashioned sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's own name stands for I or ME. 'Square' is not the dull sense but a number that is another number multiplied by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Three multiplied by three makes this number, so it is a perfect square.

clue.text: Dare America regroup to find good fellowship?

indicators.note: to regroup is to gather again in a new formation, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A challenge to the United States to pull together and rediscover a spirit of comradeship.
explanation.walkthrough: The rallying cry reads as political, but the first two words supply exactly the eleven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly mutual trust and comradeship among a group of people is what the word names.

clue.text: Quietness after peeling off, soaked in bathroom

definitions.note: a noun, while the phrase is strictly an adjective; informally it is used as a noun for an attached bathroom

indicators.note: peeling removes the outer skin, so the first and last letters are stripped away
soaked can mean drunk, and a drunk staggers about out of order

parts.note: the word with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A quiet moment after peeling off one's clothes and soaking in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaked' seems to belong with the bath, but it means drunk and scrambles the peeled letters of QUIETNESS into EN SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom attached directly to a bedroom is described with this French phrase, and informally the phrase names the room itself.

clue.text: Big screens showing a little porcine mascot

indicators.note: only a small part of the following words is shown, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Huge screens display a small pig mascot, perhaps at a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across porCINE MAScot.
explanation.definitionFit: Film theatres are often referred to by their large projection screens, a part standing for the whole venue.

clue.text: Knocks back ginger biscuit

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a critic knocks a show

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly gulps down a ginger biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks back' looks like a phrase for gulping food, but 'knocks' means criticises and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a thin, crisp, brittle biscuit flavoured with ginger, often called simply by this word.

clue.text: Critic and I regrettably offering caustic stuff

indicators.note: something done regrettably has gone wrong, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reviewer admits that the two of them sadly wrote biting, caustic notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caustic' fits the critic's sharp words, but here it is literal: a chemical that burns.
explanation.definitionFit: This strong mineral acid, HNO3, corrodes skin and metal, so it is a caustic substance.

clue.text: Nasty xenophobes with antiquated telecom facilities

indicators.note: nasty suggests something spoilt or twisted out of its proper shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unpleasant bigots are associated with outdated telephone equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of the bigots rearrange exactly into the kiosks; a phone box is the British public telephone booth.
explanation.definitionFit: Public telephone kiosks on street corners are largely obsolete now that mobiles are everywhere.

clue.text: Belittling a pair of crotchets I intone

parts.note: a minim is a note lasting as long as two crotchets
taken as written
to intone is to chant or sing

explanation.surface: A singer dismissively chants a couple of short notes.
explanation.walkthrough: A minim is the British name for a half note, worth two crotchets (quarter notes).
explanation.definitionFit: Playing something down or making it seem less important is to reduce it, a synonym of belittling.

clue.text: German lad's behind, not taking sides

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two ends, and not taking them means dropping both

parts.note: the backside, BOTTOM, without its first and last letters gives this and the final O

explanation.surface: A German boy is lagging behind, staying neutral in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' is the noun, the buttocks: BOTTOM, which loses B and M to leave OTTO. 'Not taking sides' suggests neutrality but means trim both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common male first name in Germany, as borne by Bismarck and several emperors.

clue.text: Pub's risky investment opportunity: a cider press?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the coin-operated gambling machine found in British pubs
second meaning, whimsically: a device that processes apples

explanation.surface: A pub-goer wonders whether the gamble on offer is really a cider press.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a slot machine is called this because its reels show cherries, lemons and so on; the question mark flags the jokey literal reading of a machine for fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub slot machine takes your coins on a gamble, and literally a cider press is a machine that crushes apples.

clue.text: When temperature rises, British navigator becomes a pirate

indicators.note: a rise in temperature turns cold into hot, so the letter for one is swapped for the letter for the other

parts.note: James Cook, the eighteenth-century British explorer of the Pacific

explanation.surface: A British explorer turns to piracy once the weather heats up.
explanation.walkthrough: C and H are the cold and hot labels on taps, so as the temperature rises, the C of COOK becomes H.
explanation.definitionFit: The villain of Peter Pan is a buccaneer who lost his hand to a crocodile.

clue.text: Lies in synthetic coverings

parts.note: synthetic means artificial or fake
hoods cover heads

explanation.surface: Someone is lying around wrapped in man-made fabric covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies' reads as a verb (reclines) but is the plural noun meaning untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue statements made to deceive are another way of saying untruths or fibs.

clue.text: With ten-fold increase ignored, got off

indicators.note: multiplying by ten moves one Roman numeral up to the next, so one numeral is exchanged for a bigger one

parts.note: to discount something is to disregard it

explanation.surface: Someone got off lightly when a tenfold rise in a charge was overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals C is 100 and M is 1000, so increasing C tenfold turns DISCOUNTED into DISMOUNTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who got down from a horse or bicycle is said to have alighted, the same as getting off.

clue.text: Song and dance, regularly, with beautiful Greek

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Performing a song and dance routine with a lovely Greek companion.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth she gave Theseus the thread to escape the Minotaur's labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan princess of mythology, daughter of King Minos, is a celebrated beauty from ancient legend.

clue.text: Primarily, she offers pitches ranging above normal operatics?

definitions.text: Primarily, she offers pitches ranging above normal operatics?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.words: she offers pitches ranging above normal operatics
parts.note: the initial letters of the seven words

explanation.surface: A description of a female singer whose voice reaches notes higher than usual in opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its first letters spell the answer, and the sentence itself describes the highest female voice.
explanation.definitionFit: This highest female singing voice reaches notes above the usual range, the top part in opera.

clue.text: Warrior in sad mural is never reaching the end

indicators.note: falling short of the end means the final letter of each word is never reached

parts.note: without its last letter
without its last letter
without its last letter

explanation.surface: A warrior is painted in a gloomy, unfinished wall painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The truncation applies to all three words, not just the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the hereditary military class of feudal Japan were fighters bound by a strict code.

clue.text: Antenatal routine disrupted

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown out of its usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman's regular schedule of check-ups is thrown off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antenatal routine' looks like a single phrase about pregnancy care, but it splits into definition and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means within the womb, describing the stage of life before birth.

clue.text: Public relations with a line that's been confected

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: something that has been confected

parts.note: the standard abbreviation
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spin doctor's message turns out to be made up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confected' suggests a fabricated PR line, but it is meant literally: made by a confectioner.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweet of nuts cooked in caramelised sugar is a classic confection made by sweet-makers.

clue.text: Distribute and collapse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hand round to everyone
second meaning: faint and lose consciousness

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated meanings of the same phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing leaflets round a room and fainting to the floor are both described by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: High quail, oddly plucked, in the sauce: cordon bleu?

indicators.note: high can mean intoxicated, and a drugged mind jumbles things up
plucking the odd-numbered letters away leaves only the even ones

parts.note: the second and fourth letters, once the odd ones are plucked
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gamebird served in a rich sauce, plucked and dressed, sounds like fine dining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like the French HAUTE, but it is the anagram signal; 'in the sauce' also sounds like drunk, yet is plain fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordon bleu describes cooking of the highest class, and the French phrase for elaborate gourmet cooking is an example of it.

clue.text: Old Russian leader, somewhat drastic in retrospect

indicators.note: retrospect means looking backwards, so the letters are read from right to left
somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the word is used

parts.note: the middle letters, before turning them round

explanation.surface: Looking back, an old Russian ruler seems to have been rather extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: Read drastic backwards and the answer sits inside: dRASTic.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperors of Russia before the 1917 revolution held this title, from the Latin Caesar.

clue.text: 'Talkative' singer's not so big, we're told

indicators.note: being told is hearing something spoken, so we go by sound alone

parts.note: minor means smaller or lesser; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same

explanation.surface: A chatty singer is said to be smaller than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'Talkative' hint that the singer is a bird famed for mimicking speech.
explanation.definitionFit: This Asian starling is a songbird well known for imitating human speech, hence the talkative label.

clue.text: Announced Oscar: Tango's kind of seedy

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the letters count for their sound

parts.note: Oscar and Tango are the NATO alphabet words for O and T

explanation.surface: A host reads out an Oscar winner for a seedy kind of tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' suggests sleazy, but here it literally means made of seeds or grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are cereal grains, so something tasting of or full of them is grainy, a sort of seed-filled.

clue.text: Only move us irrationally and with spite

indicators.note: acting irrationally means without logical order, so the letters lose theirs

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a speaker stirs them only through unreasoning emotion and malice.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the opening three words, all ten letters used once.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with malice or bitter hostility is behaving in a poisonous, spiteful manner.

clue.text: Sports team audibly sounded exhausted

indicators.note: audibly means in a way that can be heard, so sound matters rather than spelling

parts.note: a tired person lets out a long breath

explanation.surface: The team, worn out, could be heard groaning with tiredness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounded exhausted' reads as a description of the team, but it is the wordplay: a weary breath out.
explanation.definitionFit: A team of players lining up against opponents is commonly called this, especially in British football and cricket.

clue.text: Thoreau so moved, taking in grand country

indicators.note: to take in is to admit inside, so one piece is placed within the other
moved letters have been shifted out of their places

parts.note: taken as written
a grand is a thousand, abbreviated K

explanation.surface: The writer Thoreau was so stirred by a magnificent land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like praise for the country, but it is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars, K.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republic of Korea, whose capital is Seoul, is a nation on the southern half of the Korean peninsula.
